question: What is the primary goal of disaster monitoring in nursing?

options.A: Punishing communities for poor environmental sanitation
options.B: Constructing new buildings after an emergency occurs
options.C: Systematic observation and data collection to anticipate threats
options.D: Providing financial loans to disaster victims

explanation: Monitoring involves gathering data early to prepare for patient surges and reduce health risks before or during a crisis. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why does disaster monitoring extend into community health surveillance in Nigeria?

options.A: To collect taxes from rural health clinics
options.B: To arrest individuals who violate environmental laws
options.C: To replace traditional healers with registered nurses
options.D: To track disease outbreaks like cholera after seasonal flooding

explanation: Community monitoring catches early signs of waterborne diseases that frequently follow heavy rains and floods. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which disaster phase involves tracking real-time casualty numbers and facility damage?
explanation: The impact phase occurs during the actual event, requiring real-time tracking of casualties and immediate damage. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is monitored during the post-impact phase of a disaster?

options.A: The initial construction permits of a rural hospital
options.B: Epidemiological shifts and environmental sanitation hazards
options.C: Weather forecasts for the upcoming dry season
options.D: Seismic plate movements before an earthquake occurs

explanation: After a disaster, nurses monitor disease patterns and sanitation risks like contaminated water sources. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h2)

question: What do early warning systems primarily rely on for data collection?

options.A: Continuous feeds from meteorological and geological agencies
options.B: Patient discharge summaries from the previous year
options.C: Routine annual budget reports from the federal government

explanation: Early warning systems depend on real-time scientific data regarding weather, seismic activity, and environmental changes. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h3)

question: A sudden spike in clinic visits for watery diarrhea after heavy rains indicates what type of hazard?
explanation: Heavy rains frequently compromise water sources, leading to rapid increases in gastrointestinal infections in the community. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is syndromic surveillance used for in disaster management?

options.A: Tracking symptom patterns before a definitive laboratory diagnosis
options.B: Counting the exact financial cost of broken medical equipment
options.C: Evaluating the nursing licensure pass rates nationwide
options.D: Monitoring the daily dietary intake of hospital staff

explanation: Syndromic surveillance focuses on grouping clinical signs and symptoms early to detect outbreaks before lab tests confirm them. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why are mobile health applications useful during disaster surveillance in remote areas?

options.A: They prevent natural disasters from occurring in the region
options.B: They allow rapid transmission of health status updates to authorities
options.C: They automatically treat patients without requiring medication
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for trained nurses

explanation: Mobile tools speed up data sharing between remote clinics and central emergency command centers. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h4)

question: Which supply consumption rate must nurses actively monitor during a disaster?
explanation: Critical life-saving consumables like IV fluids and oxygen are essential targets for inventory monitoring during crises. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h5)

question: When assessing logistics for the next three days, what factor should a nurse include alongside current patient numbers?

options.A: Local market prices for food crops
options.B: The historical weather from last decade
options.D: The personal hobbies of off-duty staff

explanation: Effective logistical planning requires anticipating future patient arrivals rather than only counting those currently admitted. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h5)

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?
explanation: SBAR is a standardized communication tool used to transmit concise clinical information between health workers. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why are regular interprofessional briefings necessary during an emergency response?

options.A: To debate hospital administrative policies and salary structures
options.B: To give staff time to rest away from patient care duties
options.C: To ensure bed availability and transport logistics are shared across agencies
options.D: To replace written patient records with spoken instructions

explanation: Briefings keep all responding teams aligned on resource capacity and operational needs. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h6)

question: What ethical challenge frequently arises during disaster health monitoring?

options.A: Choosing whether to close a hospital permanently
options.B: Deciding which nurse receives a higher salary during overtime
options.C: Refusing to document patient vital signs in an emergency
options.D: Balancing public health surveillance needs with individual privacy rights

explanation: Nurses must report dangerous outbreaks to protect the public while still respecting patient confidentiality as much as possible. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h7)

question: Which type of disease reporting is mandated by public health laws in Nigeria during monitoring?

options.A: Infectious diseases like cholera and Lassa fever

explanation: Public health regulations require mandatory reporting of communicable diseases that threaten community safety. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of a post-disaster after-action review?

options.A: To discard all existing emergency response manuals
options.B: To penalize staff members who made clinical errors
options.C: To calculate annual profits for the hospital pharmacy
options.D: To evaluate monitoring effectiveness and identify operational gaps

explanation: Reviews help teams examine what worked and what failed during the emergency to improve future responses. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h8)

question: How should lessons learned from a disaster evaluation be utilized?

options.A: Integrated into updated disaster preparedness plans
options.B: Published only as academic history textbooks
options.C: Kept strictly confidential from all junior nursing students
options.D: Ignored until the exact same disaster repeats

explanation: Identified improvements must be fed back into institutional protocols to enhance future readiness. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h8)
